Roller Derby SA

By: Nicky Troll | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Fast. Full Contact. Brutal & Unexpected. Roller Derby - a sport not for the faint hearted.

Unique Selling Point:
- not widely known sport
- quirky characters
- fast paced


Summary:
Women in roller-skates, faces in war paint, fishnets and tutu wearing helmets and knee pads. It’s a sport that gained international popularity with the 2009 movie Whip It!

Further information:
From the Iron Meisies to the Sirens – these teams are not just quirky – they’re actually good and heading off to the World Champs. From Jammers to Blockers – this sport is not for the faint hearted.
THE PLAYERS
They’re not who you expect. From a maths teacher to an Actuarial Scientist – these women transform into their alter-ego on derby nights.
Samia (Sam-I-Slam) - Joburg, Actuarial Scientist/Financial Advisor
Dianne (Difibrillator) - Joburg, Financial Advisor/Insurance broker
Caitlin (CalQh8er) - Joburg, Maths teacher
Katherine (Katalyst) - Joburg, Teacher
Candice (Avada Cadaver) - Joburg, Stay at home Mom
Luami (I-maul) - Cape Town, Tattoo Artist

THE GAME
Each team comprises maximum 15 players, with up to five at a time on the track for each ‘jam’ that lasts up to two minutes. The ‘jammers’, who are the scoring players, identified with a star on their helmets, work their way through the ‘pack’ made up of ‘blockers’ and a ‘pivot’ player (stripe on helmet) from each team. The blockers’ objective is to assist their own jammer through the pack and to prevent the opposing jammer from scoring points.

ELEMENTS TO FILM
INTERVIEWS
The ladies
Samia (Sam-I-Slam) - Joburg, Actuarial Scientist/Financial Advisor
Katherine (Katalyst) - Joburg, Teacher
Luami (I-maul) - Cape Town, Tattoo Artist
** We’d want to film them in a work environment and at home
Coach:
Aimee - Iron Tyrant for the sport overview

VISUALS
Interesting transitions:
Dianne (Difibrillator) - Joburg, Financial Advisor/Insurance broker
Caitlin (CalQh8er) - Joburg, Maths teacher
Candice (Avada Cadaver) - Joburg, Stay at home Mom

** ANY FOOTAGE or PICTURES OF PAST TEAMS THAT TOOK THE WHIP IT BRIEF TO THE MAX 

FINAL SCRIPT| ROLLER DERBY

VISUAL START

VO: Not for the faint hearted, it’s an unexpectedly brutal sport.

(AIMÉE PLANK): Incredible women on skates with, like, reckless abandon.
(LUAMI CALITZ): It is a bit hardcore.
(SAMIA KUBEYA) I thought it was madness.

UPSOUND TEAM CHEER: Three, two, one! [Cheer]

(MASA): It's fast, it's fierce and it's full contact. It's an all-female sport. Think speed, skill and strength. I'm talking about roller derby.

VO: Originating in the USA in the 1930s, roller derby hit its peak before fading in the ‘70s—but rolled back into the spotlight with the 2009 film Whip It!

Today, roller derby is one of the fastest-growing contact sports for women.

VISUAL BREAK

VO: And these locals are just as relentless as their international counterparts, career women by day, athletes dominating the track by night.

At the office, a number cruncher in the insurance industry; on the track, a calculating competitor ready to take down her opponents.

UPSOUND (SAMIA KUBEYA): I’m Sam-I-Slam and I’m a blocker.

(MASA): Would you say that your daytime job and your hobby are like night and day?
(SAMIA KUBEYA): Definitely. The office is very like calm, very demure, very mindful. And derby is a lot more chaotic. But you do really focus in, I think that's one thing both spheres have, there's a great element of focus.

VO: Think rugby on roller skates—minus the ball. Instead, a player called the Jammer IS the ball, battling through a fortress of four other players known as Blockers, to rack up points on an indoor oval track.

VISUAL MOMENT

VO: Her art is permanent, and so is the impression she makes in the rink!

UPSOUND (LUAMI CALITZ): I’m I-Maul and I’m a blocker.

(LUAMI CALITZ): I first thought they were all crazy. And then I was like, I really want to do that. When I put the skates on for the first time, I was obsessed. You fall all the time, even when you get good. That's also a good life lesson to learn.

UPSOUND (KATHERINE REYES): Little Red Riding Hood, that’s right.

VO: A teacher by day, fire starter by night.

UPSOUND (KATHERINE REYES): I’m the Katalyst, the initiator of change and I’m a blocker.

(KATHERINE REYES): It speaks to the alter ego aspect of roller derby. We all have personas that we come up with, your name, your number is usually connected to this persona. And when you put on that mask, you become something else.

UPSOUND (AIMÉE PLANK): I’m (AIMÉE PLANK) Plank, I’m also the Iron-Tyrant and the head coach of Team South Africa

(AIMÉE PLANK):We’re kind of told to take up a little less space, be a little less loud. You have to teach them how to be aggressive, how to, yeah, take a hit, give a hit It's beyond just this really fun, cool sport that's like outside the norm, it's what it teaches us .

VO: In July, Team SA will be taking their skills to the 2025 World Championships in Austria, their third appearance on an international track.

(AIMÉE PLANK):We're going to face teams where we're not going to stand much of a chance. We're going to face teams that we're really going to give them a big run for their money. But it's,it's more about getting people to know that we are here at the bottom of Africa, playing this incredible sport, making it happen, and that we’re growing.

VO: But the sport is still quite niched in South Africa, with just two major teams in Cape Town and Johannesburg.

(AIMÉE PLANK):Funding is a big thing. We're completely self-run, self-funded. But for us, we're teaching people from the minute they sit in these stands. Okay, so this is how the game works - you see this person, that’s what they’re doing. And the fans that stick around long enough to start figuring out how it works - really, really enjoy seeing how it plays out.

(MASA): I guess the best way for me to understand the sport is to lace up.

(MASA): All right. OOOH. WHOOOOH.
(AIMÉE PLANK): Hi.
(MASA): Hi AIMÉE! I need help. Okay.
(AIMÉE PLANK):All righty.
(MASA): Let's just start with the basics.

(AIMÉE PLANK): Okay. Side to side. Beautiful. yeah, yeah, Keep that bum out - you’re going to get to the other side.
(MASA): WHOOOHOOO! [laughing]
(AIMÉE PLANK): You got it! You got it! Yeah!
(MASA): It's harder than I thought.

(AIMÉE PLANK): So in a game of roller derby, you have two teams. Each can have up to 15 skaters. But we play two minute jams within our bout, which is what we call a game. And every two minutes we would field five skaters, one jammer that wears a star on their helmets and four blockers, one of which with a pivot cover that can assist their jammer.

VO: Each team has their own wall of blockers on the track - they play both defence—obstructing the rival jammer—and offense, creating opportunities for their own jammer to break through.

(AIMÉE PLANK): Blockers sets. Go!

(AIMÉE PLANK): The jammer is in pink. Wearing the helmet cover with the star. That is your point scorer, and she is trying to fight through the other team's wall of blockers
(MASA): Geez!
(AIMÉE PLANK): Every time she passes one pair of opponent blockers hips. She gets some points.
(MASA): I can't believe she got past it.
(AIMÉE PLANK): Yeah, it's really physical.
(MASA): It’s hectic!
(AIMÉE PLANK):It's really hard work // there's four against one.
(MASA): Yeah!
(AIMÉE PLANK): So it's all about that agility, about that speed, about that strength. We need to squidge out of the way here.
(MASA): Okay. Whoa! [Laughing] Firing line!
(AIMÉE PLANK): And you were ready to get into the game I see!
(MASA): I was just trying to block as well.
(AIMÉE PLANK):Natural, natural talent!

VO: It might look like a street fight on wheels, but roller derby is coordinated and tactical.

(SAMIA KUBEYA): It's very fast paced, Jammers take big hits on the line. Skating is hard work, especially because there's quite a bit of lateral movement as well, which is a bit difficult on quad skates. So it's a full body workout.

VO: It’s controlled chaos with rules—break them, and you’re off to the sin bin.

(AIMÉE PLANK): Because of the nature of the sport, we can't just kind of play prison rules and just let anybody hit you anywhere. So we have a lot of rules to keep our players safe. We can’t be injuring them. We can't kick them. We can't hit them below their knees. You can't hit people in the middle of the spine. As with any sport, things don’t always happen according to plan, we have penalties if you do an illegal contact.

VO: There’s more at play than just big hits — it’s about endurance, and teamwork.
And for Katherine, Roller Derby wasn’t just a sport—it was survival.
(KATHERINE REYES): So my daughter, at the age of 11, had Ewing's sarcoma, which is a rare form of bone cancer. And after 15 months of battling, she passed away. I don’t think anybody does grief the same way. And dor me, it was just transmuting that physical pain into something tangible. So the anger I felt about her passing. The unfairness of life, you know, you take it to the track. And in a contact sport like that, you just can’t get hit hard enough.

VO: The roller derby rink is a battleground, empowering women to stand strong.

More than anything, this sport is about showcasing regular women doing extraordinary things… on roller skates.

(KATHERINE REYES): People from all walks of life that you would never have spoken to before, or you never thought maybe you had something in common, and now you just kind of band together and you realize that the bonds you make on that track are unbreakable. Because when you have a group of people with you telling you: pick yourself up, telling you: dust yourself off, telling you go for it. It just gives you so much fire and so much, so much confidence and power.

VO: It’s not just about the competition. It's about resilience and proving what's possible.

(SAMIA KUBEYA): What would my life be like without roller derby? I'm worried. I’d turn into a workaholic. Like, it's a nice space for me to turn off my brain and focus on doing something else.

(LUAMI CALITZ) I think one big thing that I learned from roller derby and roller skating in general is just that sometimes it's okay if you want to do something that you're really bad at, if you’re having fun and you persevere, eventually you’ll get better.

UPSOUND ROLLER DERBY PLAYERS CHEERING

(KATHERINE REYES): It's given me an opportunity to love myself. And through this crazy contact sport where I thought, oh, I need to get in here to get over my hurt. It’s made me healthier, I’ve built muscle, I’ve built friendships. Life without roller derby would be very, very sad.

END

metadata.Further information: From the Iron Meisies to the Sirens – these teams are not just quirky – they’re actually good and heading off to the World Champs. From Jammers to Blockers – this sport is not for the faint hearted. THE PLAYERS They’re not who you expect. From a maths teacher to an Actuarial Scientist – these women transform into their alter-ego on derby nights. Samia (Sam-I-Slam) - Joburg, Actuarial Scientist/Financial Advisor Dianne (Difibrillator) - Joburg, Financial Advisor/Insurance broker Caitlin (CalQh8er) - Joburg, Maths teacher Katherine (Katalyst) - Joburg, Teacher Candice (Avada Cadaver) - Joburg, Stay at home Mom Luami (I-maul) - Cape Town, Tattoo Artist THE GAME Each team comprises maximum 15 players, with up to five at a time on the track for each ‘jam’ that lasts up to two minutes. The ‘jammers’, who are the scoring players, identified with a star on their helmets, work their way through the ‘pack’ made up of ‘blockers’ and a ‘pivot’ player (stripe on helmet) from each team. The blockers’ objective is to assist their own jammer through the pack and to prevent the opposing jammer from scoring points.
